binding_constraint.reason: The type-aware JSON walker is the single mechanism every Tier 2 observable behavior runs through (echo, timestamps-in-JSON, ID-in-JSON, size-bound enforcement, cycle detection). It must simultaneously preserve JS types, emit deterministic key ordering, detect cycles, bound size incrementally, AND ship without breaking the existing string-mode path (headers, URL, query). If the walker does not exist or blows its p99 budget, every other RT becomes unreachable regardless of how elegantly the helpers, enhancer, or provider fixtures are designed. RT-2 (compile-time factory closure) is the mechanism by which RT-1 scales within the 5ms budget, so its correct shape is a sub-property of RT-1's viability.

tension_validation.note: Compile-time factory + JSON-body-only walker + incremental size tracking keep hot path within ~3.35ms headroom; honors P1+P10+P11 as resolved.
Provider coverage is a test-layer decision (RT-7); Option C does not change the 5+1+1+1 regression surface.
Dual walker explicitly segments by context: JSON-body → type-preserving, headers/URL/query → string-mode. This is EXACTLY U2's validated-by-pre-mortem resolution.
Factory closure materialises seeded PRNG per-request (nanoid customRandom + Mulberry32); IDs are deterministic AND regex-valid — the composite P40 resolution.
Walker and helper surface are provider-agnostic by design; provider names never enter src/. RT-9 adds the CI grep gate.
Shared spec parser module + --spec flag for enhancer live in RT-6; Option C's walker does not touch this seam.
`_mockstarGenerated` boundary is in the enhancer (RT-6), not the walker; Option C preserves the contract.
Compile-time output is a factory closure per placeholder; RT-2 encodes this directly, and RT-1 consumes it.
Walker carries cumulative byte-count state; short-circuits to 413 before serialisation. Sub-truth RT-1.5 codifies this.

draft_required_truths.draft_statement: A type-aware JSON templating engine must exist that (a) parses response templates as JSON-with-placeholders (not text); (b) walks request.body preserving JS types (number, string, bool, null, object, array) on substitution; (c) produces deterministic key ordering; (d) has cycle detection and max-recursion-depth.

A dual-mode ID generator must exist: nanoid-with-custom-alphabet in non-deterministic mode (CSPRNG-backed via crypto.getRandomValues), and a seeded PRNG (Mulberry32 or equivalent) scoped per-request in deterministic mode. Both paths produce IDs matching the provider regex with 0 collisions over 1M draws at length 14.

A `mockstar enhance <dir>` command must exist that reads existing imported mocks, detects the provider/format version, rewrites response bodies in place with Tier-2 placeholders, is idempotent, preserves user-made post-enhancement edits, and refuses unknown format versions with a clear error.

All provider-specific behavior must be expressible through generic helpers. Core contains zero provider-name conditionals; provider-shaped examples live under examples/mocks/<provider>/ as documentation of how the primitives compose.

The template evaluator must be a sandboxed grammar evaluator with no access to process / filesystem / network / eval. Malformed request bodies must not crash the process; they must produce structured error responses.

A cross-provider regression test harness must exist, exercised in CI on every commit, covering Razorpay (5 endpoints) + Stripe (≥1) + Twilio (≥1) + PayPal (≥1), asserting ID shape, request echo, timestamp freshness, and deterministic-mode byte-identity.

The templating contract must distinguish JSON-value context from string context. JSON-body templates are type-preserving; header, URL, and query-string templates remain string-mode (preserves existing behavior so Tier 2 is not a breaking change for non-JSON-body templates).

gap_checklist_compliance.note: Core data path: HTTP request → matcher → template context build → helpers evaluated → JSON walker substitutes placeholders type-preservingly → response serialize → send. Each transition covered by T1 (budget), T3 (walker correctness), S1 (error isolation), O2 (regression tests per endpoint).
Narrow scope: S2 requires CSPRNG for ID generation. No auth surface in Tier 2 (no crypto signing, no session, no session-token validation).
S4 (bounded echo response size) and T14 (cycle detection + max depth) address amplification and unbounded recursion. Mockstar core already has a body-size limit at the HTTP layer.

gap_checklist_compliance.skip_reason: Tier 2 is entirely in-process. No external HTTP dependencies, no DNS lookups, no external API calls during request handling.

gap_checklist_compliance.note: S1 (malformed body graceful) + T8 (missing field fallback) + T12 (field-mapping rules) cover the input validation surface. Content-Type checking is inherited from mockstar core's request parser.

T6 (100 parallel unique IDs) + T10 (PRNG state per-request, not process-global) address concurrency. T3's walker is stateless per request; no shared mutable state. Templates compile once at config-load (T5); eval is pure-function.

iterations.result: Discovered 34 constraints across 5 categories (4 B / 15 T / 4 U / 5 S / 6 O). Pre-mortem surfaced 8 new constraints (T11, T12, T13, T14, T15, S5, O5, O6) plus validated 2 existing (U2, T10) marked via validated_by_pre_mortem flag. Context lookup grounded T2 (Razorpay 14 confirmed; Stripe 'opaque ≤255' reshapes claim; Twilio 34-char hex; PayPal 17-char uppercase) and T3 (Mockoon bodyRaw pattern is prior art). User extended cross-provider regression scope from Stripe-only to Stripe+Twilio+PayPal (B4). 7 DRTs seeded for m3.

9 tensions surfaced and resolved — 5 trade_offs (TN1/TN3/TN4/TN5/TN7/TN9), 1 resource_tension (TN2), 2 hidden_dependencies (TN6/TN8). TRIZ classification per tension: 8 exact-match parameter pairs (speed-vs-correctness, simplicity-vs-capability, standardisation-vs-flexibility, performance-vs-reliability, speed-vs-safety), 1 approximate (TN4 — reproducibility-vs-authenticity, nearest match 'global vs local optimum'). All 9 passed propagation check — zero VIOLATED effects. Resolutions converged on segmentation (P1) as the dominant principle across 6 tensions, with prior-action (P10) and beforehand-cushioning (P11) for the performance ones. Two genuine design choices resolved via AskUserQuestion: TN6 → enhancer re-parses source spec; TN7 → `_mockstarGenerated` top-level key as the generated/user boundary (user explicitly requested a tool-name, not a manifold-internal name like `_tier2*`). 2 hidden_dependencies become blocking_dependencies for m3.

Derived 9 required truths from the outcome's 4 observable behaviors. RT-1 (type-aware JSON walker with cycle detection, deterministic key ordering, incremental size tracking, string-mode preservation for non-JSON contexts) identified as BINDING CONSTRAINT — RT-2/RT-4/RT-5/RT-6/RT-7/RT-8 all depend on it. Recursive decomposition to depth 2 surfaced 6 sub-truths of RT-1 (RT-1.1 placeholder parser, RT-1.2 type-preserving substitution, RT-1.3 cycle + max-depth, RT-1.4 deterministic key ordering, RT-1.5 incremental size bound, RT-1.6 string-mode dual path). Both blocking_dependencies from m2 (T12→T7, T5→T10) flow into RT-6 and RT-2 respectively, validating the m2 handoff. 4 solution options generated; Option C (hybrid JSON-walker for body + unchanged string-template for headers/URL/query) recommended — REVERSIBLE_WITH_COST, satisfies all 9 RTs, CONFIRMED by all 9 m2 tensions. Option B (full engine rewrite) and Option D (fork into dynamic-json schema) are ONE_WAY and deprioritised. RT-9 (provider-agnostic core) is SPECIFICATION_READY — current src/ has zero provider references per baseline grep; just needs a CI grep gate to enforce going forward. RT-2 and RT-8 are PARTIAL because mockstar core already has compile-at-load (CompiledJsonValue, finding F3) and per-request try/catch (S1 baseline), but the factory-closure shape (RT-2) and sandbox invariant test (RT-8) are new.
